2
At temperatures close to 0 K, the specific heat capacity c of a particular solid is given by c = bT 3,
where T is the temperature and b is a constant, characteristic of the solid.
The SI unit of specific heat capacity is J kg–1
K–1.
What is the unit of constant b, expressed in SI base units?
A
m2
s–2
K–3
s–2
K–4
B
m2
s–2
K–3
C
kg m2
s–2
D
kg m2
K–4

hints: Notice the equation $c = bT^3$, so the units must satisfy unit of $b$ = unit of $c$ divided by unit of $T^3$, where $T$ is in $\text{K}$.
Recall that the joule is not a base unit: $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$, so first rewrite $\text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$ in $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$ and $\text{K}$.
Divide that base-unit form of $c$ by $\text{K}^3$ and combine the powers of $\text{K}$ to get the unit of $b$.
walkthrough: Start from homogeneity: $c = bT^3$ means $[b] = [c]/[T^3]$, with $[T] = \text{K}$ so $[T^3] = \text{K}^3$.
Write $[c] = \text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$ in base units using $\text{J} = \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$.

A.explanation: Gives $\text{K}^{-3}$ instead of $\text{K}^{-4}$ because it omits the $\text{K}^{-1}$ already in the unit of $c$ when dividing by $T^3$.

B.explanation: Follows from $b = c/T^3$ with $c$ in $\text{m}^2\text{s}^{-2}\text{K}^{-1}$, giving $\text{m}^2\text{s}^{-2}\text{K}^{-4}$.

C.explanation: Keeps $\text{kg}$ and gives $\text{K}^{-3}$, so it fails to cancel $\text{kg}$ against $\text{kg}^{-1}$ and to include the $\text{K}^{-1}$ from $c$.

D.explanation: Keeps $\text{kg}$ because $\text{J}$ was not fully expanded to $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$ and cancelled against $\text{kg}^{-1}$ in $c$.
